correctness.rationale: For the Petersen graph KG(5,2), explicit full cellular chain groups have ranks 45,120,75. The embedded verifier reconstructs every boundary sign and verifies d1*d2=0. It enumerates exactly 12 graph pentagons and six disjoint pairs and their 25-square product cycles. It checks all six boundaries vanish and their reoriented integer sum is zero. Exact mod-3 elimination gives rank(d2)=70, while five independent kernel cycles bound its rank above by 70, hence H2=ker(d2) has free rank 5 and no degree-three boundaries. A specified 5x6 minor of the six cycle chains has every 5x5 column deletion determinant ±1, proving integral saturation and that any five form an integral basis. All 120 S5 graph automorphisms act on these cycles by unsigned permutation after the specified reorientation; Sylow-five subgroup identification is enumerated. The nonsplitting argument uses transitivity and integral averaging. No finite extrapolation or uncertain numerical rank is used.

value.rationale: Integral equivariant structure and geometrically meaningful homology generators are not determined by a Betti number or rational irreducible character. The six Petersen pentagon decompositions form a canonical symmetry-complete family; the result identifies exactly how their embedded tori generate top homology, a unique primitive relation, and a nonsplit S5-permutation-lattice extension. The all-five-subsets unimodular certificate is a natural integral rigidity statement, not an arbitrary numerical slice, and gives a concrete usable basis and action for future graph-braid calculations.
